# Vendored code

Code in this tree that this repository did not author, with where it came from.
The rule it serves is STANDARD.md VN1: a file the author did not write is
traceable to a declared source, or it is not vendored, it is just present.

`tokens/check.mjs` (`checkVendored`) holds this file and the tree to each other:
every file under a vendored root is listed here, and every path listed here
exists. Adding a component without recording it fails the gate.

## components/ui — shadcn/ui

**Upstream.** The shadcn/ui registry (`https://ui.shadcn.com`), generated by its
CLI. The generating configuration is `components.json` at the root: style
`new-york`, base colour `neutral`, RSC on, TSX on, CSS variables on, icon library
`lucide`. Those settings are the closest thing to a version this import recorded.

**Upstream commit: not recorded.** This is the gap this file admits rather than
papers over. The components were generated before any provenance rule existed, and
the registry stamps no version into the files it writes, so the exact upstream
revision is not recoverable from the tree. It is not invented here. Going forward,
the rule in VN1 is that a component added or re-pulled records the registry
revision on the line it is added to — the first re-pull is what makes this section
true rather than honest-but-empty.

**Imported.** 2026-07-28, commit `f3c4d55`, all in one commit.

**What is actually pinned.** The registry copies source; the behaviour lives in the
primitives underneath, and those are exact-pinned in `package.json`: 27
`@radix-ui/react-slider` and `@radix-ui/react-slot`, both pinned without a range
character, plus `embla-carousel-react` 8.6.0. So the API surface the surviving
files bind is versioned even though the files themselves are not.
`class-variance-authority`, `tailwind-merge`, `clsx`, and `lucide-react` carry
`^` ranges.

The other 33 packages this root used to pull in — 25 more `@radix-ui/*`, `cmdk`,
`input-otp`, `react-day-picker`, `react-hook-form`, `react-resizable-panels`,
`recharts`, `sonner` and `vaul` — went with the files that imported them. None was
reachable from a route.

**Locally modified — 1 file.** This is the fact a manifest exists to carry, because
an upgrade that overwrites it loses work silently:

| File | Change | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| `components/ui/carousel.tsx` | Adds a `viewportClassName` prop so a caller can bleed the `overflow-hidden` clip outward and stop card shadows being clipped at the edge; sets `strokeWidth={1.5}` on both arrow icons. | `17d4d87`, 2026-08-03 |

Re-pulling `carousel` from the registry drops both. Re-apply them, or move the
viewport escape hatch into a wrapper so the vendored file goes back to pristine.

**Unmodified — 2 files.** Byte-identical to what the CLI wrote, by git history:

`components/ui/button.tsx`, `components/ui/slider.tsx`

**53 files removed.** The registry generated 55 unmodified components; 53 of them
were reachable from no route, config, test or content file in this repository, and
STANDARD.md H2 says a file referenced by nothing is deleted. They are gone, with
the two shadcn support hooks (`hooks/use-mobile.ts`, `hooks/use-toast.ts`) that
only they used. Git history is the record if one is ever wanted back; the registry
regenerates any of them in a command.

That the clause had been stated since the standard existed and nothing measured it
is the reason 53 files accumulated. `checkReachability` in `tokens/check.mjs` now
evaluates H2 on every gate run, so the next unreferenced file fails in the change
that adds it.

## components/ame/icons — Swiss Confederation icon set

**Upstream.** A Storybook export of the icon set published by the
Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft (Swiss Confederation), MIT licensed. The raw
export is `components/ame/icons/icon-source.html`; `scripts/parse-ame-icons.mjs`
reads it and writes `icon-data.ts`, normalising each glyph to inherit
`currentColor` and leaving the path data otherwise unchanged. 218 glyphs.

**Licence.** MIT. It permits this use — including redistribution inside an
Apache-2.0 tree and commercial use — on one condition: the copyright and
permission notice must be included in all copies or substantial portions. 218
glyphs is a substantial portion, so the full text is reproduced in
`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` and clause L1 reads it on every gate run. A condition
that survives only while nobody deletes a file is not a condition.

**Upstream revision: not recorded.** The same gap this file admits for
`components/ui`, and admitted here rather than papered over: the export carries
no version stamp. A re-pull records the revision on the line that adds it.

**What is this repository's, and stays Apache-2.0.** The React wrapper
(`icon.tsx`, `icon-fallback.tsx`), the fallthrough to `lucide-react` for names
the set does not carry, and the generator. The shapes are the upstream's; the
machinery around them is not.

**How this was found.** It was not found by the gate. The licence audit that
moved this tree to Apache-2.0 asked what a licence actually asserts, and the
icons had no recorded provenance at all — they were simply present, which is
the exact condition VN1 exists to make impossible and did not catch here,
because `components/ame/icons` was not a declared vendored root. It still is
not; the provenance is recorded and the licence condition is enforced by L1,
but the structural gap that let 218 third-party files sit unrecorded is real
and is not closed by this entry.

## Not vendored, but living under a vendored root — 5 files

These are this repository's own components, sitting in `components/ui` because that
is where they were written, not because anyone decided they belonged there. They
carry no Radix primitive and no registry counterpart; `glass-button` reads this
repo's own `.port-glass` language, which no upstream ships.

`components/ui/avatar-counter.tsx`, `components/ui/glass-button.tsx`,
`components/ui/layered-card-stage.tsx`,
`components/ui/sync-card.tsx`

**Why this matters more than the filing.** R-8 exempts `components/ui` from the
naming clauses (N2/N3), from eslint, and from the uses-graph, on the stated ground
that "its names are the upstream's call, not this repo's". For these 4 that ground
is false: the names *are* this repo's call, and the exemption is excusing code the
standard should be holding. The exemption is over-broad by exactly 5 files: `layered-card.tsx` was the sixth and went with the unreachable files, since nothing reached it either.

Recorded, not fixed, in this pass: moving them is an import rewrite across every
call site, which is its own order and cannot be reviewed alongside a provenance
manifest. The classification above is by name against the shadcn registry and by
inspection for Radix imports, not by diff against upstream — the upstream revision
being unrecorded is the same gap this file opens with.
